messages.subject: B Allele Frequency graph interpretation
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I started using the Sequenza tool to look at whole exome data from FFPE.
I had a question regarding the raw profile figure in the "whole_genome_view.pdf".
Even with sample having very low to no CNV change, my B allele frequency does not show the heterozygous positions (or I think its the scaling of the figure). Attached you can find the figure.
I was wondering what might cause this (I also wonder if it is a technical issue or an FFPE problem). If it is a scaling problem, where can I change this parameter because I went through the Sequenza package documentation and there was no description of the function that generate this "raw profile".
I would appreciate any help
Thanks.
Best,
Tincy

messages.body_plain:

I noticed that in all my analysis, information is completely missing from the beginning (p arm) of the chromosomes 13,14,15,21,22. Interestingly, I see this with all the graphs provided through the publication of Sequenza. I was wondering why does this happen?
Best,
Tincy

messages.subject: Re: missing information in beginning of chromosome 13,14,15,21,22
messages.subject_clean: missing information in beginning of chromosome 13,14,15,21,22
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tincy,

it’s because those are acrocentrics chromosomes, and the initial part of the chromosome is basically a big gap for the centromere and heterochromatin.

you can check also from the gap database
http://hgdownload.cse.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/hg19/database/gap.txt.gz

I’m sure you should be able to get something from the p arm anyway, but the reference for it is completely masked with Ns

try: samtools faidx genome.fa 13:10000-16000000  | less

All thing considered, it’s quite a chunk of the genome missing, probably there is something important there we don't know yet :).

Best

Francesco

messages.subject: Copy number calling variability when the depths of normal/tumor pair differ
messages.subject_clean: Copy number calling variability when the depths of normal/tumor pair differ
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I tried Sequenza on 9 whole exome samples.

Three of them did not give me accurate results with respect to copy number calls (I tried initially CNVkit to get the copy number information and used batched normal, basically pooling all the normals together, to provide a control for the analysis).

One of the samples that dropped out was, I would say due to cellularity issue. sequenza predicted cellular content of less than 30%. I read in the paper that this might happen with samples with low cellularity.

But the other two had really good cellularity (in the 80% range).

>From the previous reponses in this group, I read that if the depth ratio within a region fluctuate a lot, this might be an indicator of why the copy number calling is wrong.

I checked this and attached you can see that this is indeed the case for one of the samples and not the other.

Both samples tumor ran at a mean depth of ~40X while the normals ran at ~70X.

Could this depth difference be the reason contributing to the wrong calls?

I do want to point out Sequenza accurately called copy number for the rest of 6 samples when compared to CNVkit and gave me more info I couldn't have received from CNVkit!

Best,
Tincy

messages.subject: Extract A- and B-allele Copy Number from defined genomic windows.
messages.subject_clean: Extract A- and B-allele Copy Number from defined genomic windows.
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I've ran sequenza on multiple samples from the same tumor and realised that the "segments" printed in *segments.txt are not exactly the same between samples.
For instance:

SampleA:
chr1 861360 120529750 0.498945460101109 1526 0.0818170728566135 1.00587035477684 150304 0.347476456672401 2 1 1 -6.75347986806467

SampleB:
chr1 861360 1148504 0.49956130190539 11 0.159435766490344 0.975186126715064 4645 0.230308828067809 2 1 1 -6.73331440122957

chr1 1246303 26900735 0.498947424983779 699 0.0804295503438109 0.917306455048607 86098 0.304506586454427 2 1 1 -7.14993565738541

chr1 27058036 120529750 0.498943251975809 856 0.0923180731643665 0.971394449604164 157433 0.351126068942888 2 1 1 -6.74630131709021

As you can see, there is only one segment being called in SampleA, while there are 3 in SampleB (even though they have exactly the same CN "genotypes" for A and B allele) for the same genomic interval.

Since I'm trying to compare the results in all samples,  I would like to ask whether there is an option to get the A- and B-allele CN for the same genomic windows? In other words, can you pre-define your genomic windows of interest and then call the CN genotypes on them?

Thanks in advance,
Joao

messages.subject: Re: Extract A- and B-allele Copy Number from defined genomic windows.
messages.subject_clean: Extract A- and B-allele Copy Number from defined genomic windows.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joao,

yes, you can define breakpoints in the extract step (bypassing the built-in segmentation).
You need a data.frame file with 3 columns: chrom, start.pos end.pos.
Then, when you run sequenza.extract you use the object with the breaks option:

    my_breaks <- read.table(“my_curated_bed_file.txt”, header=F, sep=“\t”, stringsAsFactor=FALSE)
    colnames(my_breaks) <- c(“chrom”, “start.pos”, “end.pos")
    test <- sequenza.extract(my_seqz_file, breaks=my_breaks)

Unfortunately there isn’t a easy way to automatically provide the “right” segmentation for the 2 samples, I usually end up doing a visual inspection with chromosome.view and manually curate the breaks in the segments file

There are multi-sample segmentation options, but not with the allele frequency taken into account.

Francesco
